To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
histone acetylation and/or histone variant influences the nucleosomal DNA lengths.

we sequenced both ends (5' and 3' ends) of mononucleosomes and dinucleosomes of Aspergillis fumigatus after treatment with trichostatin-A (TSA) and showed that most of the genes were not affected by TSA treatment.

the histone deacylase inhibitor TSA elongated the nucleosomal DNA and the dinucleosomal DNAs of A. fumigatus cells, and the locations where nucleosomes were frequently detected in the promoters of the genes were highly conserved between the cells treated with TSA and the untreated cells, even though the nucleosome locations in the bodies of the genes were not conserved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nucleosome organization of the genome of A. fumigatus and the effects of the histone de-acetylase inhibitors on the nucleosome organization.
the nucleosome positioning and histone modifications in A. fumigatus.
the nucleosome positions in the gene promoters and bodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nucleosome positions and the DNA lengths are influenced by histone modifications and variants, especially in the regions with high nucleosome densities.
histone modifications, and/or histone variant influence the nucleosomal length, but not nucleosome positions.

histone acetylation is a major factor in the elongation of the DNA fragments, and the elongated DNA fragments are not distributed randomly in the genome, but are distributed according to their nucleosome positions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleosome positioning is conserved in the promoters of the genes and the nucleosome positioning in the bodies of the genes are affected by the histone acetylation.
the nucleosome positions of the gene promoters are more conserved between the untreated cells and TSA-treated cells, compared to the gene bodies.
TSA influences the density of the nucleosomal DNAs, and that this change is conserved in the promoter regions, but not in the gene bodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleosome positions of the gene bodies are more sensitive to TSA than those of the gene promoters.
the nucleosome positions of the regions with higher density of nucleosomes are influenced by the treatment with TSA.
the histone modifications and histone variants influence nucleosomal DNA length, but not nucleosome positioning in the gene promoters.
